Question: What is the most awkward moment that happened to you due to your clothes?
Answer: Couple of decades ago, me and my friend were traveling with a company to London. Once we were there we found out that we were going to eat at a fancy smancy club which had served Madonna just few days ago and then we would go out and party and a fancy club. Me and my friend were just two young computer nerds, so we decided we needed to go out and buy suits and all. Went to a place called Brook’s brothers or something like that and they were going out of business, so we could buy some nice suits for not that much money. Each of us got help and we were measure back and forth independently. I saw my friend in his suit and said to my helper that he had the type of suit I would like, more than the colors he had been showing me. A little tayloring here and there, we paid and left. We went in our suits and partied. After we had eaten we went to the fancy club. For some reason or another, people kept asking us where the toilets were. A few times is just fine but this was happening quite frequently, all too often. Finally we asked another co-worker if he was being asked where the toilets were? Nope, not even once. One of us asked him then why we were constantly asked this question, was it because we were not seemingly drunk? No, he said laughing so hard he was crying. You are wearing the same suit. So, it turns out, we bought identical suits and did not notice, not even when we were together. People thought we worked there

Question: What's the best computer/laptop to buy for programming and coding?
Answer: If the operating system does not matter, nothing beats a Macbook. Be it Air, Air 15 or any of the Pro machines. Nothing comes close. Sure you can calculate trillion Fibonacci values more in a few milli seconds on other computers but it is the full package that matters. Nothing comes close. But if it does, and you prefer Intel/AMD machines. Thinkpads are always nice. Not the Thinkpads with a name attached to them like Yoga, the ones with 1 letter, numbers and optional letter, like P15v, W something. Those are amazing. Dell XPS works great as well. If you want to be different, Acer makes a kickass machines called Predator. They don’t have much battery life to speak of, but they sure pack a lot of things in them and they tolerate to be dropped and kicked, or as Norwegians would say, a little “juling”. There are also new computers with the Intel Ultra chip. They are not exactly powerhouses but they are above good, great battery life and are generally quite nice.
